newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares oblivious to falls elsewhere.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares oblivious to falls elsewhere.

text.p: Portuguese shares were oblivious to the drops in foreign markets, and the PSI-20 index of 20 leading stocks ended higher, led by rises in 'blue chips' such as industrial group Sonae Investimentos and cement group Cimpor. Dealers said they expected the market to rise further in coming sessions, although they expected a quiet day tomorrow as many foreign investors were absent due to the New Year holiday period.
* PSI-20 index up 0.12 percent to 5,152.34 points.
* "The fundamentals of the market are good and it has potential to rise," said one operator.

* Dealers said the rise in Cimpor was due to the positive outlook for the firm's performance. "Cimpor is cheaper than Semapa (its main rival)," said one dealer. Dealers said expectations that Cimpor would acquire another cement company boosted the stock.

* Sonae Investimentos hit an all-time high of 5,030 escudos on optimism over its recently announced restructuring, an improved forecast for the group's 1996 results and strong prospects for the company's performance.
